subject: Long-context summarization: regression follow-up & pilot proposal
messages:
From: Sana Iqbal <sana@meddelta.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Barnes <oliver@meddelta.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — long-context behavior

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo earlier — helpful to see Redwood's runtime and the summarization examples. A few notes from our side:

- Our primary use case is visit-note summarization across patient histories that average ~25k tokens, with outliers up to ~80k tokens.
- We saw summarization truncation in the sample outputs you showed when we pushed the tail cases. Fidelity dropped on medication history and event ordering.
- Our security team will need SOC2 artifacts but that's a separate thread — I'll share contacts if required.

Can you recap what model variants you think are the best fit for us (balancing latency and quality), and whether Redwood can run a targeted pilot on ~500 notes with our prompt set? If possible, include a simple mutual action plan and an estimate of cost/time.

Thanks — Sana
Sana Iqbal
Head of Clinical ML, MedDelta

Attachments: meddelta_example_batch.zip (3 sample notes), meddelta_sample_schema.csv
From: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — long-context behavior

Hi Sana — really glad the demo was useful. Quick recap and a proposed next step plan below. I'll also loop Neha for prompt/eval specifics and Rishi for any performance/quant ops.

Summary of fit:
- Recommended model family: mix of Llama-3-70B-Chat (8k native) with RedQuantized-70B-8K-Long variant for throughput, plus a Longformer-optimized 70B variant (RedLong-70B-64K) for tails where fidelity matters.
- Why: The RedQuantized variant gives ~2.3x token-cost reduction on our standard benchmarks with small latency impact; RedLong-70B-64K preserves ordering and long-range attention patterns for multi-visit timelines.

Observed risks (from today's samples):
- Truncation: notes > max-context are currently downsampled via suffix-drop in the demo pipeline, which loses final event entries. We can instead use prefix+sectioned KV caching to maintain key early events and the last 8k tokens; requires runtime tuning.
- Regression risk: if we switch quantization profiles aggressively we may see hallucination on date/medication entities — we'll validate this in the eval.

Proposed pilot (500 notes):
1) Intake: Secure S3 transfer of the 500-note batch + schema (you've attached samples; we'll request full batch link). Timestamp: 1 business day to provision.
2) Baseline: Run your current summarizer (you'll provide outputs) vs. 3 Redwood variants: RedQuant-70B (fast), RedLong-70B-64K (high-fidelity), and R3-13B-Structured (low-cost).
3) Eval: We run automated metrics (ROUGE-L, entity F1 for medication/date, and order-preservation score) and hand-grade 50 high-risk notes. We'll provide a regression matrix for each model/quant profile.
4) Ops: 2 weeks pilot with rolling checkpoints (day 3, 7, 14).
5) Deliverables: benchmark report, prompt set (initial suggestions), recommended production config and estimated token cost.

Estimated effort & cost: ~2 FTE-days to configure + 300 GPU-hours on dedicated infra; we estimate $8k-$12k in usage for the pilot depending on variant mix.

Next steps:
- Please confirm you can provide the 500-note S3 link and the canonical prompt set you want us to test.
- If acceptable we'll schedule an internal kickoff (30 min) on Friday to finalize the mutual action plan.

Attachments included: redwood-benchmark-report.pdf (2026-07 long-context baseline)

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0173

Adding a bit more color from an eval/prompt perspective. Aisha — feel free to forward to Sana after you review.

Prompt & eval notes:
- Prompt set: We should include 3 prompt families: (1) extraction-first (schema-first bullet lists), (2) timeline-centered (explicit instructions to preserve chronology), and (3) compression-summary (short patient-safe summary). I've attached a starter prompt JSON (sample_prompt_set_v2.json).
- Metrics: besides ROUGE and entity-F1, use a "chronology accuracy" metric that measures pairwise event ordering preservation. For medication fidelity, use a normalized string-match + manual adjudication on a 50-note sample.
- Regression checks: run A/B with and without aggressive q4_0 quantization; flag any entity F1 drop > 4 pts as a potential regression. Also watch hallucination rate (non-existent med/date) > 2%.

Operational notes:
- For the pilot, enable persistent KV cache across notes in the same patient to emulate real-world conversation context. We can approximate with a 2-pass strategy: long-read pass to extract timeline anchors, then summarize with anchors as context. This reduces token waste and preserves ordering.
- I'll prepare an eval spreadsheet where we log model/quant profile rows + metrics + flagged regressions. Linking to the sheet below.

Related links:
- Prompt set (starter): https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/meddelta/long-context-prompt-sets
- Benchmark draft: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/long-context/2026-08-meddelta-report
- Eval sheet (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/meddelta/eval-2026-08

I recommend starting with RedLong-70B-64K for the high-fidelity path and RedQuant-70B for cost baseline; the 13B variant can be used to iterate quickly.

Neha Kapoor
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference
